questions.stem: How is the genetic material in a bacterial cell organised differently from that in a human cell?

options.text: Bacterial DNA is circular and free in the cytoplasm; human DNA is linear and enclosed in a nucleus
Human cells have DNA but bacterial cells use RNA instead
Bacterial DNA is enclosed in a nucleus; human DNA is free in the cytoplasm
Both bacterial and human DNA are organised in exactly the same way

questions.explanation: Bacterial cells have a single circular chromosome that floats freely in the cytoplasm in the nucleoid region. Human cells have linear chromosomes enclosed within a membrane-bound nucleus.
